options.label: A
options.latex: Is a present value of the annuity.

options.label: B
options.latex: Uses the previous result to obtain the next value in the annuity investment.

options.label: C
options.latex: Uses the final result to obtain the next value in the annuity investment.

options.label: D
options.latex: Is the addition of future and present value of the annuity.

solutions.latex:
A recurrence relation gives each term from the term before it, for example $A_{n+1}=A_n(1+r)+M$ for an annuity investment.

So it uses the previous result to obtain the next value.

Option A and option D describe a present value or a sum of values, not a rule linking one term to the next, and option C uses the final result, which is not known when the relation is applied.
$$\therefore\ \text{the statement that uses the previous result to find the next value is correct}$$
criteria: Correct answer

meta.self_check: Definition of a recurrence relation compared with each option.

solutions.latex:
The table gives the present value of an annuity of $\$1$ per period. For $6\%$ and $3$ periods the factor is $2.6730$.

Multiply by the payment of $\$5000$.
$$\begin{aligned} PV &= 5000\times 2.6730\\ &= \$13365 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{the present value is } \$13365$$
criteria: Correct answer

solutions.latex:
The loan is the present value of all repayments. The rate per month is
$$\dfrac{6\%}{12} = 0.5\% = 0.005$$
Treat the repayments as $\$500$ for all $48$ months plus an extra $\$300$ for the last $24$ months (months $25$ to $48$).

The factor for the last $24$ months is the difference of the $48$ and $24$ period factors at $0.005$:
$$42.58032 - 22.56287 = 20.01745$$
$$\begin{aligned} \text{PV} &= 500\times 42.58032 + 300\times 20.01745 \\ &= 21\,290.16 + 6005.235 \\ &\approx \$27\,295.40 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{Louise can borrow a maximum of about } \$27\,295.40$$
criteria: Correct answer
Sets up the present value with correct factors and amounts for both repayment periods, or equivalent merit
Identifies the rate $0.005$ per month and the factors $22.56287$ and $42.58032$, or equivalent merit

meta.generated_note: Used the difference of the table's 48 and 24 factors for months 25 to 48, which equals the deferred annuity.

parts.latex:
Present value interest factors for an annuity of \$1 for various interest rates and time periods are given in the table below.

\extable{828_q39_t1}

Isaac uses this table to calculate his car loan repayments. His loan is \$24 500 and will be paid in equal monthly payments. The monthly interest rate for his loan is 0.7%.

Calculate the how much Isaac will save paying back the loan in 2 years instead of 3.

solutions.latex:
For 2 years there are $24$ payments, with table factor $22.0216$.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Instalment} &= 24500 \div 22.0216 \\ &= \$1112.544\ldots \\ \text{Total} &= 1112.544\ldots \times 24 \\ &= \$26\,701.06 \end{aligned}$$
For 3 years there are $36$ payments, with table factor $31.7247$.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Instalment} &= 24500 \div 31.7247 \\ &= \$772.268\ldots \\ \text{Total} &= 772.268\ldots \times 36 \\ &= \$27\,801.68 \end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Savings} &= 27\,801.68 - 26\,701.06 \\ &= \$1100.62 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{Isaac saves } \$1100.62$$
criteria: Correct answer
Correctly calculates one total repayment and finds both instalment amounts, or equivalent merit
Identifies both interest factors and finds the instalments, or finds one total repayment amount, or equivalent merit

The table gives the present value interest factors for an annuity of \$1 per period, for various interest rates (r) and numbers of periods (N).

\exfigure{2846_q3a_1}

A man plans to invest \$200 each month for 6 years. His investment will earn interest per month at the rate of 9.6% per annum.

Based on the information in the table, what is the present value of this annuity?

solutions.latex:
Monthly payments for $6$ years give $n = 6\times 12 = 72$. The monthly rate is $r = \dfrac{9.6\%}{12} = 0.8\% = 0.008$.

From the table, the factor for $n=72$, $r=0.8\%$ is $54.57097$.
$$\begin{aligned} PV &= \text{factor}\times\text{amount} \\ &= 54.57097\times 200 \\ &= \$10\,914.19 \end{aligned}$$
This matches option B.
criteria: Correct answer

parts.latex:
An annuity consists of ten payments, each equal to \$2000. Each payment is made on 30 June each year from 2021 through to 2030 inclusive.

The rate of compound interest is 5% per annum.

The present value of the annuity is calculated at 30 June 2020.

The future value of the annuity is calculated at 30 June 2030.

Without performing any calculations, which of the following statements is true?

solutions.latex:
Payments total $10\times 2000 = \$20\,000$. The present value is calculated before the payments, so interest has not yet added to them: each payment is discounted, giving less than $\$20\,000$.

The future value is calculated at the last payment, so earlier payments have earned interest, giving more than $\$20\,000$.
$$\text{Present value} < \$20\,000 < \text{future value}$$
This matches option D.
criteria: Correct answer

What would be the Present Value (PV) of this annuity?

solutions.latex:
The rate is $\dfrac{6\%}{2}=3\%$ per half year, and the number of periods is $3\times2=6$.

The table intersection is $6.4684$.
$$\begin{aligned} FV &= \$2500\times6.4684 \\ &= \$16\,171 \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Correct answer
Uses other intersection factor, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
Use the future value formula $FV=PV(1+r)^n$ with $r=0.03$ and $n=6$.
$$\begin{aligned} PV &= \dfrac{FV}{(1+r)^n} \\ &= \dfrac{16171}{(1+0.03)^6} \\ &\approx \$13\,542.96 \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Correct answer (mark awarded if the calculation is correct for an incorrect value from part (a))
